items.title: GDB Holdings buys 51pct stakes in two firms for RM81.6mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: GDB Holdings Bhd is acquiring 51 per cent stakes in two construction companies for RM81.6 million. In a bourse filing, GDB said it will acquire 51 per cent of Bina Tegas Sdn Bhd for RM66.51 million and 51 per cent of BT Borneo Engineering Sdn Bhd for RM15.09 million. GDB will satisfy the RM81.6 million consideration through RM40.8 million cash and RM40.8 million of new GDB shares.

items.title: ‘Tonto’ pleads not guilty to 55 bribery charges totalling RM62,900 involving traffic police
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — A ‘tonto’ (lookout) pleaded not guilty at the Sessions Court here today to 55 charges of giving RM62,900 in bribes to three traffic police officers between January 2022 and February 2026. According to the charges, the man was alleged to have corruptly given money to three traffic police officers from the Petaling Jaya District Police Headquarters, Negeri Sembilan Contingent Police Headquarters and the Kesas Expressway EMPV Patrol Office, as an inducement for them not to inspect lorries during roadblocks. The bribes were allegedly given in several transactions at several bank branches in Klang and Setia Alam, involving amounts ranging from RM700 to RM2,000.

items.title: Ringgit ends higher against Asean currencies, lower versus US dollar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The ringgit closed higher on Thursday against most Asean currencies, but lower against the US dollar amid a renewed surge in oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions in Middle East, an analyst said. At 6pm, the ringgit inched down to 4.0890/0940 against the greenback from Wednesday's close of 4.0850/0895. At the close, the ringgit traded mixed against a basket of major currencies.

items.title: Haze turns Sun blazing red over Johor
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI: The sun appeared blazing red over Johor today as haze blanketed the state, creating a striking sight across the skies. Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) director-general Dr Mohd Hisham Mohd Anip said the phenomenon was caused by the scattering of visible light by haze particles in the atmosphere. "It means tiny haze particles in the air bend and spread sunlight, making the Sun appear red or orange.

items.title: 'Education, Health ministries must meet on measures for haze-forced school closures'
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Education and Health ministries need to meet immediately to find the best measures for school closures brought on by the haze enveloping the country. Its president, Associate Professor Datuk Dr Mohamad Ali Hasan, said the association respected the royal decree, which expresses concern for the safety and health of students as they face unhealthy air quality readings. Ali said the safety and health of pupils and students must be prioritised, as haze can have adverse effects on health.

items.title: Malaysia, Myanmar agree ministries must act together on refugee cooperation, says PM Anwar
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Myanmar agree that relevant ministries and agencies need to take coordinated and proactive action to advance bilateral cooperation, including efforts to address the issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said this was emphasised during his meeting and bilateral talks with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today. He said following their joint press conference, he and Min Aung Hlaing attended the Malaysia-Myanmar Cooperation Dialogue at Kompleks Seri Perdana, organised by the Institute of Strategic and International Studies (ISIS) Malaysia.

items.title: [UPDATED] Haze: MoE institutions with API above 180 to shut from tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: All educational institutions under the Education Ministry (MoE) in areas recording Air Pollutant Index (API) readings above 180 will be closed from tomorrow. Education director-general Datuk Dr Mohd Azam Ahmad said this followed a decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, over pupils' safety and health amid the haze. "All educational institutions under MoE in areas recording API readings above 180, based on readings recorded by the Department of Environment (DoE), must be closed from Friday.

items.title: Exsim Hospitality bags RM15.6mil building works contract
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Exsim Hospitality Bhd's unit Exsim Concepto Sdn Bhd has clinched a RM15.62 million subcontract to supply and install building services and undertake general building works. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, Exsim Hospitality said the subcontract works, awarded by Nestcon Builders Sdn Bhd, began today and are scheduled for completion on Oct 31, 2028. Exsim Concepto is principally involved in specialised fit-out services for hospitality property assets, general contracting and centralised procurement.

items.title: NRD issues 169,346 new generation MyKads nationwide in three weeks
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Oct 8 — The National Registration Department (NRD) has issued a total of 169,346 New Generation MyKads nationwide between September 17 and October 6. NRD Director-General Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias said the five states recording the highest issuance are the Federal Territories with 20,592 pieces; Johor (18,871); Sarawak (15,777); Sabah (13,711) and Selangor (13,452). Also present was Terengganu NRD Director Awatif Hannan Md Yusup.

items.title: Viral park fight leads police to detain 13 students in Tawau
items.summary: TAWAU: Police have detained 14 individuals, including 13 students, to assist in investigations into an armed brawl involving a group of teenagers at a park in Taman Ambar, Jalan Kuhara, here. Tawau district police chief Assistant Commissioner Rosdi Mat Jusoh said all those detained, aged between 12 and 14, were picked up by the Tawau police headquarters Criminal Investigation Department yesterday. Police received a report on the incident at 6pm two days ago.

items.title: MARKET PULSE PM OCT 8, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia extended its losses ahead of the 2027 Budget, with investors turning more cautious as surging oil prices and heightened geopolitical tensions clouded the market outlook. The benchmark index fell nearly 11 points to 1,601.01. In the crypto market, Bitcoin fell further to RM341,076.

items.title: Thailand starts extradition proceedings against Chinese journalist who exposed corruption
items.summary: BANGKOK: Thai authorities began extradition proceedings on Thursday against a Chinese investigative reporter wanted by Beijing and detained for months in Thailand, his lawyer and an official told AFP. Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Lin Jian said in July that Bai was suspected of extortion and bribery, and an extradition request had been submitted to Thailand. He said the process could take months.

items.title: Fatal highway crash: Trailer rams stalled car on NSE, triggering fire
items.summary: MUAR: A 43-year-old man was killed after a trailer rammed a stalled car on the southbound stretch of the North-South Expressway early today. District police chief Assistant Commissioner Raiz Mukhliz Azman Aziz said the victim, a front passenger, died after the Proton Wira was struck by the trailer and dragged forward before bursting into flames. Raiz Mukhliz said the driver and another passenger managed to get out of the car before it was dragged forward by the impact and caught fire.

items.title: Anthony Loke: RTS Link not delayed, buffer time needed for safety approvals
items.summary: JOHOR BAHRU, Oct 8 — Malaysia and Singapore jointly decided to start the Johor Bahru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link operations in February 2027, rather than taking a unilateral step, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said. The minister said the approvals involved Malaysia’s Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) and Singapore’s Land Transport Authority (LTA). He said RTS Link operations could start as early as January, but February was chosen to provide a buffer and ensure safety evaluation and technical approvals proceed smoothly.

items.title: SUV driver fined RM4,000 for tailing Zahid Hamidi’s police convoy on Kesas
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — A property agent was fined RM4,000 by the Magistrates’ Court here today after pleading guilty to disobeying a police order by following the convoy escorting Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi yesterday. He subsequently paid the fine. Earlier, a video went viral showing an SUV driver following a police convoy escorting the Deputy Prime Minister from Kajang towards Sunway Medical Centre in Subang Jaya.

items.title: HI Mobility's unit to continue serving Johor Baru's residents with stage buses
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: HI Mobility Bhd's subsidiary, Handal Indah Sdn Bhd, has received a letter of intent (LOI) from the Land Public Transport Agency (APAD) for its proposed appointment as the network operator under the stage bus service transformation (SBST) programme in Johor Baru. In a statement, HI Mobility said the non-binding LOI allows Handal Indah to engage with APAD, an agency under the Transport Ministry, on its continued participation in the SBST programme. The proposed appointment is in line with Handal Indah's expertise in smart mobility, fleet management and public transport operations.

items.title: Malaysia must strengthen regional cooperation to ensure stable energy supply, says Akmal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia has highlighted the need to strengthen regional cooperation to ensure a stable and affordable energy supply, alongside efforts to accelerate the transition to low-carbon energy. In a statement, the Ministry of Economy said that the Azec collaboration complements the implementation of the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR), including energy efficiency, renewable energy, green mobility, infrastructure development, and transition financing. Earlier, Akmal Nasrullah also held a bilateral meeting with Josh Wilson, the Deputy Climate Change and Energy Minister from Australia’s Department of Climate Change, Energy, the Environment and Water, focusing on energy supply security and gas supply between the two countries.

items.title: Retiree loses RM70k to scammers posing as police
items.summary: The victim lodged a police report yesterday after discovering that seven cash withdrawals had been made from his account without his knowledge. District police chief Superintendent Roslan Mohd Talib said the victim was contacted by suspects who claimed he was involved in a money-laundering case. "The victim then found seven cash withdrawals were made without his knowledge, resulting in losses totalling RM70,000," he said in a statement today.

items.title: Kelantan warns: Dogs without anti‑rabies vaccination tags may be culled
items.summary: BACHOK, Oct 8 — Dogs without vaccination tags or that have not received anti-rabies vaccinations after April each year may be culled by local authorities in Kelantan to curb the risk of rabies transmission. State Local Government, Housing, Health and Environment Committee chairman Hilmi Abdullah said the provision is in line with the Kelantan Anti-rabies Vaccination Order, which requires owners to ensure their pet dogs are vaccinated between January and April every year. “This year, 21 dogs in Bachok have been vaccinated, while samples from another 20 dogs have been taken for rabies testing,” he said.

items.title: Nestlé, Food Bank extend food aid partnership
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nestlé (Malaysia) Bhd and Yayasan Food Bank Malaysia (YFBM) have extended their food redistribution partnership for another three years, focusing on reducing food waste and supporting communities in need. Nestlé Malaysia has contributed more than RM7 million worth of products through food redistribution and humanitarian relief initiatives carried out with YFBM to date. Nestlé Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the partnership would allow surplus products to be redirected to communities that need them.

items.title: Mustapha seeks higher Sabah, Sarawak development funds
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Sabah and Sarawak Affairs Minister Datuk Mustapha Sakmud hopes the 2027 Budget will maintain or slightly increase development allocations for Sabah and Sarawak. Sabah still needed substantial funding for basic infrastructure, particularly for recurring floods, road and water issues, he said. The Sepanggar MP also called for the Auditor-General's recommendations on the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway to be acted upon immediately and used to improve project management.

items.title: Three Pontian siblings killed in motorcycle‑lorry crash after insisting on school despite haze closure
items.summary: PONTIAN, Oct 8 — Unconvinced that the school had been closed due to the haze today, an elder brother eventually gave in to his two younger siblings’ insistence on going to school on a motorcycle, before all three were killed in an accident at Jalan Kampung Parit Haji Siraj, Kayu Ara Pasong, here, this morning. The victims’ mother, Julaiha Munaji, 44, said that her two children, Nor Daniel Fikri Norlizan, 11, and Puteri Naufa Raisha, eight, still wanted to go to Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Parit Sapran, despite being informed that the school had been closed due to the haze. She said that they did not believe that the school had been closed, with one of them even reportedly pleading to go to school, while wearing their school uniform and preparing their schoolwork.

items.title: Nurse stabbed 6 times by husband previously reported death threats to police
items.summary: KOTA BARU: The 44-year-old nurse who was stabbed six times by her husband at their home in Kampung Padang Lepai near Kadok on Monday had lodged a police report in August after he had threatened to kill her. A relative who declined to be named said the victim had been seeking a divorce after six years of marriage following repeated threats by her husband whenever they argued. The relative said the victim lodged the report at the end of August and had since stopped living with the 47-year-old husband.

items.title: Quarantine, unease and rumours: Russian city grapples with plague scare
items.summary: WHEN a woman died of suspected plague in Siberia last week, Oksana was in the maternity ward for observation. "Everything was fine, and then they told us that a woman had died. And they wouldn't let anyone in or out," the 35-year-old told AFP.

items.title: Bursa Malaysia ends lower amid higher oil prices, geopolitical risks
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended lower today, remaining under selling pressure ahead of 2027 Budget announcement tomorrow, as a renewed surge in oil prices and escalating geopolitical tensions in West Asia further dampened risk sentiment. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 10.77 points to 1,601.01 from Wednesday's close of 1,611.78. Turnover decreased to 3.51 billion units worth RM3.46 billion, compared with 3.83 billion units worth RM3.52 billion yesterday.

items.title: GEAR-uP to build Malaysia's capital pipeline
items.summary: "This calls for a connected investment ecosystem where capital, expertise and institutional support work together," an observer said. However, they said GEAR-uP's longer-term value extends beyond the capital deployed. In 2025, RM2.6 billion was deployed through investment vehicles designed to bring private capital alongside government-linked funds.

items.title: Private jet operator CGT Asia denies wrongdoing, says four released after questioning
items.summary: CGT Asia Limited's lawyer Kitson Foong said the company had never authorised the transportation of drugs or other illicit cargo. He said all four who were detained had fully cooperated with investigators. Foong said the aircraft which departed Subang for Luang Prabang, Laos, on Oct 1 had not been carrying any cargo when it left Malaysia.

items.title: Manufacturing firm fined RM30,000 over workplace accident, safety breaches
items.summary: The company was fined an additional RM2,500 each on two charges of failing to report the serious injury to the nearest Department of Occupational Safety and Health (DOSH) office immediately and failing to submit an accident report within seven days. The charges were brought by Penang DOSH under Section 15(1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act 1994, punishable under Section 19 of the same Act, and Regulation 5(1)(b)(aa) and Regulation 5(1)(b)(bb) of the Occupational Safety and Health (Notification of Accident, Dangerous Occurrence, Occupational Poisoning and Occupational Disease) Regulations 2004. "Employers have a legal responsibility to ensure the safety, health and welfare of workers, including providing safe work systems and identifying and controlling occupational safety and health risks," Penang DOSH said in a statement.

items.title: MISC secures 20-year charters for five new LNG carriers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MISC Bhd has secured long-term time charters for five newbuild liquefied natural gas (LNG) carriers from Petronas LNG Ltd (PLL), with each vessel contracted for 20 years. MISC will provide the LNG shipping services through its wholly owned subsidiaries," it said. MISC said the project would enable it to capitalise on Petroliam Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) anticipated growth in LNG production while supporting the renewal of its LNG carrier fleet.

items.title: Steven Sim: Tourism surge and foreign fans drive RM345m SME gains from Bahrain F1 GP
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Local micro, small and medium enterprises (MSME) reaped over RM345 million in economic spillover effects of the Bahrain Gulf Air Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix (GP) at Sepang International Circuit. Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim Chee Keong added that almost half of the 261,000 spectators were foreign tourists. “The impact reflects the important role of large-scale international sporting events in stimulating economic activities, especially through the rise in tourism expenditure and demand for local goods and services.

items.title: MMA: 63pc MO reporting rate in Sabah, Sarawak may not reflect ground staffing
items.summary: MMA president Dr Sivanaesan Letchumanan said the association had taken note of the Health Minister's announcement that about 63 per cent of MOs offered permanent placements in Sabah and Sarawak had reported for duty. He said public healthcare doctors could work continuously for 33 hours when placed on on-call duty. he said.

items.title: Bank sell-off casts pall in Southeast Asia, Singapore stocks drop 3pct
items.summary: BENGALURU: Major banks in Southeast Asia declined more than one per cent on Thursday, with the region's top lender, DBS Group, dragging Singapore stocks more than three per cent lower as rising bond yields brought into focus risks to bank earnings growth and funding costs. The MSCI EM Asia equities index declined 1.8 per cent in its worst day since early September, largely weighed down by a 2.6 per cent drop in South Korea's KOSPI. In Singapore, the FTSE Straits Times Index shed as much as 3.2 per cent to hit its lowest since mid-July, with DBS dipping 5.2 per cent to mark its steepest daily loss since April last year.

items.title: Drivers warned against high beams, hazard lights during haze
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Drivers have been advised against using high beams and hazard lights while driving in haze or thick fog, as reduced visibility can increase the risk of accidents. The advice came from a coalition of road safety non-governmental organisations comprising the Road Safety Expert Association (RSEA), Malaysian Eminent Persons on Road Safety Forum Group (MEPORS) and Road Safety Alliance Malaysia (ROSAM), as part of a public service campaign. The coalition said high beams could reflect off airborne particles during haze, creating glare and further reducing visibility.

items.title: After 39 years, Sri Kumar prepares for life beyond the police force
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: After nearly four decades of confronting armed criminals, protecting world leaders, training elite police commandos and managing national crises, Datuk M.V. Sri Kumar is preparing to hang up his uniform. When marathon runners see the finish line, they are excited.

items.title: Dzulkefly: Food Bill proposes publishing non-compliant food information without court order
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government has proposed expanding the powers of the Director-General of Health to publish information on food that does not comply with the Food Act 1983 (Act 281) or regulations made under it, without a court order. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the proposal under the Food (Amendment) Bill 2026 would allow such information to be published through print or electronic media in the interest of public safety. He said the 39-clause bill also proposed amendments to Section 12 of Act 281 to allow convictions under the act to be published through print or electronic media.

items.title: AGC objects to former Tabung Haji chairman Abdul Azeez’s bid to challenge IRB over RM4.8m tax settlement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Attorney General’s Chambers (AGC) has objected to former Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) chairman Datuk Seri Abdul Azeez Abdul Rahim’s application for leave to commence judicial review proceedings against the Inland Revenue Board (IRB), over its alleged unilateral cancellation of an agreement on the settlement of RM4.8 million in tax and penalties. Ng said the impugned letter stated that a review of the case had uncovered new findings and facts concerning income allegedly omitted from the agreement, resulting in the cancellation of the agreement and consequently, the composite assessment with a new tax computation to be issued in due course. “Abdul Azeez was not directed by the impugned letter to pay any additional tax.

items.title: RTS Link construction unaffected by Anthony Loke resignation
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Construction of the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link will proceed as scheduled despite Transport Minister Anthony Loke's decision to resign from the Cabinet. Also present was Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh. Loke said on Sept 29 that he had submitted his resignation as a Cabinet minister to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.

items.title: Negri Sembilan 2027 Budget to be tabled on Nov 27, says MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Negri Sembilan state government will convene the state legislative assembly on Nov 26, followed by the tabling of the state's 2027 Budget on Nov 27, said Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. Ismail said the absence of state executive councillors (Exco) would not affect preparations for the budget, as the state government could make decisions on the budget without the Exco. Ismail said the state government would consult all 25 government assemblymen on the budget this month, adding that the views of all elected representatives would be taken into account in its preparation.

items.title: Nhaveen murder trial: Accused admits taunting victim, denies assault
items.summary: "I saw Previin and Nhaveen at the burger stall. Tatisan and I taunted Nhaveen, but I cannot recall what was said. Ragesuthen testified that while at Jalan Kaki Bukit, Previin and Nhaveen arrived on a motorcycle and asked Tatisan why he was taunting Nhaveen, before Previin allegedly struck Tatisan with a helmet.

items.title: Witness tells court he handed RM350,000 in cash to Hamzah Zainudin’s former aide over PDRM tender
items.summary: Wan Azhar Mohamed Yusof, 51, said he handed over RM100,000 to Sayed Amir Muzzakkir at about 4pm on December 4, 2020, and RM250,000 at 3.30pm on December 16, 2020. The 17th prosecution witness said this when re-examined by Deputy Public Prosecutor Hazel Tan Jia Qi at the trial of Sayed Amir Muzzakkir, who is facing three corruption charges involving RM350,000 in connection with a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) project tender. Wan Azhar also confirmed that Sayed Amir Muzzakkir had asked him, “Can you pay 350k?

items.title: US ambassador to Greece sought US$100,000 from donor: WSJ
items.summary: ATHENS: The United States' Ambassador to Greece, Kimberly Guilfoyle, sought US$100,000 from a donor and offered access to top administration officials, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday. Guilfoyle offered to use her sway to help Trump donor Eric Deters on tax and legal issues, and asked him to pay a US$100,000 bill she owed American Express, according to the Journal. Please," she reportedly said in Signal messages to Deters.

items.title: MyDCD signs underwriting agreement with TA Securities ahead of ACE Market listing
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MyDCD Bhd has signed an underwriting agreement with TA Securities Holdings Bhd ahead of its proposed listing on Bursa Malaysia's ACE Market. The company is undertaking an initial public offering (IPO) comprising 335 million new ordinary shares and an offer for sale of 145 million existing shares. The 145 million existing shares under the offer for sale comprise 79.34 million shares for selected investors and 65.66 million shares for selected Bumiputera investors approved by the ministry, both through private placement.

items.title: Why Malaysian professionals look to Singapore? Because many can earn more than double, says HR minister
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysian professionals could earn significantly higher working in neighbouring Singapore compared to just a median income of around RM6,000 here, according to a study, highlighting a stark wage disparity that Putrajaya is seeking to address through targeted tax incentives and wage growth initiatives. By contrast, a study by government agency TalentCorp showed that a majority of Malaysian professionals employed in Singapore earn between SG$4,001 (RM12,773) and SG$7,000 (RM22,348) per month. Malaysian professionals earning the national median wage of RM6,124 per month are typically subject to a standard personal income tax rate of 19 per cent.

items.title: Jelutong MP urges govt to provide financial assistance to families of Malaysians missing in Nepal floods
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The government has been urged to consider providing financial assistance to all Malaysian families whose relatives are still missing due to the floods and landslide disaster in Nepal last August. The matter was proposed by Jelutong Member of Parliament RSN Rayer, who also urged the relevant departments or ministries to consider a moratorium on housing loans, personal bank loans, and vehicle purchases for all victims involved. PHEB Deputy Chairman Senator Dr. R.A. Lingeshwaran said eligible families can apply for the assistance via a QR code displayed on PHEB’s official Facebook account and website.

items.title: E-hailing driver claims trial to driving under influence of drugs, causing Maldivian student’s death on LDP
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — An e-hailing driver today claimed trial in the Magistrate’s Court here to three charges, including causing the death of a Maldivian student in an accident on Sunday. The first charge was framed under Section 44(1)(a) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum prison term of 15 years and a fine of between RM50,000 and RM100,000 upon conviction. The third charge, under Section 43(1) of the act, carries a maximum prison term of 12 months and a fine of between RM5,000 and RM10,000 upon conviction.

items.title: Malaysia needs highly skilled talent to support shift to high-value economy, says Zambry
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 8 — Malaysia needs skilled talent to support its transition to a high-value economy, Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir said. He said the country has several policies and plans to develop highly skilled talent, including the Malaysia Higher Education Blueprint 2026-2035, the 13th Malaysia Plan and the National Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) Policy 2030. Zambry said INDEX is more than a platform that brings institutions and industry together; it connects industry needs with the strengths of higher education.

items.title: National Climate Change Bill to institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting, says Arthur Kurup
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The proposed National Climate Change Bill will institutionalise mandatory carbon accounting and clear governance to give businesses the legal certainty needed to decarbonise. Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability (NRES) Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the legislation, alongside the National Climate Change Policy 2.0, would align Malaysia’s environmental agenda with the National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) and New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030). He said the measure would also strengthen investor confidence and encourage domestic and international investment in clean technologies.

items.title: Anwar personally contacts Indonesian President Prabowo over haze crisis
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said today he has personally contacted Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto regarding the “alarming” level of transboundary haze affecting Malaysia and the region. “The matter of the haze is at an alarming level and I’ve personally contacted President Prabowo, and he has agreed to take the necessary steps,” Anwar said. His remarks come as the Department of Environment (DOE) reported that 38 areas in Malaysia recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index readings at 3pm today.

items.title: Selangor govt, state Education Dept to discuss measures to address haze and Super El Nino, says MB
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 8 — Selangor Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari will meet the State Education Department (JPNS) tomorrow to discuss follow-up measures regarding the haze situation currently affecting the state. He said the meeting would look into the necessary measures, including those involving school operations, based on developments in air quality and reports from the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) and Department of Environment (DOE). “I will meet JPNS tomorrow to look at what immediate follow-up measures we can take.

items.title: King calls for schools to close if API stays above 150-180 for prolonged period
items.summary: The King expressed concern over the health and safety of schoolchildren and students amid the haze affecting the country, urging the Education Ministry to give serious attention to the situation. “Appropriate measures must be taken by the relevant ministries and agencies to protect schoolchildren and students, including senior citizens and patients with respiratory illnesses. Sultan Ibrahim stressed that the health and safety of schoolchildren and students must be given priority amid the deteriorating air quality.

items.title: Dapat Vista responds to PAC findings, backs urgent completion of formal eJamin agreement
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Dapat Vista (M) Sdn Bhd, the operator of the eJamin court bail payment system, has acknowledged the findings and recommendations of the Public Accounts Committee and supports the urgent completion of a formal agreement with the government. The company, a subsidiary of Pertama Digital Berhad, said the agreement would strengthen accountability and enhance safeguards for bail funds while maintaining continuity of service for the courts and the public. “Public confidence matters to us, and we continue to take our responsibility to bailors seriously,” the companies said.

items.title: Hazy math: DoE explains why your AQI says 250 when the official API is 175
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Department of Environment (DOE) has clarified that higher air quality figures displayed on independent mobile applications and third-party websites do not reflect data suppression or inaccuracies in official records Just as 38 areas in Malaysia logged unhealthy air quality today, the department explained that Malaysia’s Air Pollutant Index (API) and commercial Air Quality Index (AQI) platforms frequently show divergent numbers because they rely on different index scales, mathematical models, concentration thresholds, averaging durations, update intervals, and sensory inputs. Satellite monitoring, the DOE pointed out, evaluates total aerosol column density across the upper atmosphere rather than air quality at ground level where human respiration occurs. Unhealthy air quality blankets 38 areas As of 3pm today, no monitoring stations in the country recorded good air quality, with 30 stations registering moderate levels and 38 falling into the unhealthy category (API 101 to 200).

items.title: Zambry: MOHE targets 30,000 AI graduates by 2030 to meet future workforce needs
items.summary: Its Minister Datuk Seri Zambry Abdul Kadir said the target would be achieved through 30 specialised programmes at bachelor’s, master’s and doctoral (PhD) levels currently offered at 11 public universities. He said to ensure that academic programmes remained relevant to technological advancements, 455 programmes across various levels had undergone a review as of Sept 30. “For specialised AI programmes, development and accreditation have also been strengthened through the Programme Standards: Artificial Intelligence (PS:AI) developed by the Malaysian Qualifications Agency (MQA), to ensure that they are developed systematically and meet the stipulated quality standards,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat today.

items.title: Malaysia strengthens space disaster SOPs, prepares for risk of falling space objects, says Chang Lih Kang
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Malaysia is strengthening the country’s preparedness to deal with potential incidents involving falling space objects, including satellite or rocket debris, through simulation exercises and improvements to disaster operating procedures. Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Chang Lih Kang said the effort included the implementation of the Space Accident Simulation Exercise (ExLAKA), which serves as a platform to test and assess the country’s response capabilities in the event of a space object falling incident. He said the assessment results and findings from the overall exercises would be used to improve the Space Disaster Standard Operating Procedures (PTO) 4.0.

items.title: King grants audience to IPCC chairman at Istana Negara
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, today granted an audience to Independent Police Conduct Commission (IPCC) chairman Datuk Zolkopli Dahalan and deputy chairman Martina@Kartina Zamhari at Istana Negara here. “His Majesty also received a briefing on the statistics of complaints that the IPCC received, as well as the status and outcomes of cases that have been resolved,” according to a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page today. The commission also makes recommendations to improve the welfare and wellbeing of police personnel.

items.title: Myanmar president departs Malaysia after two-day visit focused on repatriation, bilateral ties
items.summary: SEPANG, Oct 8 — Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing departed for home this afternoon after concluding a two-day official visit to Malaysia. Min Aung Hlaing, who arrived yesterday, was accorded an official welcome at the Perdana Putra Complex in Putrajaya this morning. During the meetings, Malaysia and Myanmar agreed to strengthen bilateral ties, prioritise people-centric cooperation, and support Myanmar’s efforts to pursue reforms and policy adjustments aimed at addressing the country’s complex challenges.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng urges Anwar to deliver tangible economic relief, raise tax threshold to RM12,000 in likely ‘final’ pre-election Budget
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — Bagan Member of Parliament Lim Guan Eng has urged Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to use Budget 2027 to deliver tangible economic relief, calling it the administration’s final realistic opportunity to win over voters before the next general election. Lim proposed raising the personal income tax relief threshold to RM12,000 from the current RM9,000 to offset cumulative inflation, noting that the relief limit has remained unchanged for 17 years. Lim said that while he believed Anwar could still table the Budget before Parliament is dissolved, any attempt to win over voters would not be as effective as “it would be too late”.

items.title: Anwar-Min Aung Hlaing talks focus on refugees, not recognition of Myanmar govt, says Fahmi
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU, Oct 8 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s meeting with Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing today does not constitute recognition of the country’s government but is aimed at resolving the longstanding issue of Myanmar refugees in Malaysia. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the meeting reflected the government’s use of diplomatic channels to address domestic concerns, particularly those involving Myanmar refugees. “This meeting does not mean we recognise the Myanmar government.

items.title: Loke urges Malaysian ports to speed up green transition with electric terminal trucks
items.summary: ISKANDAR PUTERI, Oct 8 — Domestic port operators have been urged to accelerate their decarbonisation initiatives, including the adoption of electric terminal trucks (e-prime movers) for port operations, said Transport Minister Anthony Loke. Meanwhile, Loke commended the consolidation of PTP and Pasir Gudang Port under the ‘Johor Port’ brand, which he said had helped the combined port operations achieve a ranking of 11th among the world’s busiest ports. He said Johor’s port facilities, comprising PTP and Pasir Gudang Port, handled more than 14 million containers annually.

items.title: Malaysia to strengthen AI training modules as deepfake, scam risks grow, says Gobind
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 8 — The Digital Ministry will continue to strengthen its artificial intelligence (AI) training modules based on newly identified risks, including deepfake threats and the misuse of the technology. Its Minister Gobind Singh Deo said the effort was being carried out through AI Malaysia Bhd, which also has an AI Safe initiative involving experts to examine security aspects and identify preventive measures against emerging technology threats. Responding to a supplementary question from Tan Hong Pin (PH-Bakri) on the role of AI Malaysia Bhd in expanding AI talent and skills development, particularly among youths, Gobind said the effort required collaboration among various parties, including the Ministry of Education, Ministry of Higher Education, industry and academic institutions.
